reading.body:
Four AWS facilities cluster within a few hundred meters of each other in Madison County, Mississippi, making that single county the entirety of Mississippi's tracked data-center footprint.

The tight geographic spacing, with longitude values differing by less than 0.005 degrees across all four sites, suggests a campus arrangement rather than four independent locations. Campus builds of this kind are common when an operator acquires adjacent parcels to stage successive construction phases, sharing power infrastructure, cooling resources, and physical security across a contiguous boundary.

The dataset records no megawatt figures for any of these facilities, so nothing can be said about their power draw, capacity, or contribution to Mississippi's grid load. The absence of MW data is a significant gap for any analysis linking Mississippi's data-center presence to AI compute capacity or regional electricity demand. The record covers only what is built or permitted as of the generation date, and does not indicate whether additional operators have announced projects in the state.
